overprovisioned-steady.description: A flat load on a workload that asks for far more than it uses. The easy case: every tool should find the waste and none should disturb the service.

diurnal.description: A day/night cycle compressed into 60 minutes, repeated. Sizing for the trough breaks the peak; sizing for the peak wastes the trough.

step-increase.description: Load triples at minute 40 and stays. Measures reaction time and whether a tool that shrank the workload earlier hurts it now.

spikes.description: A flat base with four 3-minute bursts at five times the load. Measures stability: a good tool neither ignores them nor oscillates.

steady-growth.description: Load grows 1% of the base per minute, doubling over the run. Measures whether a tool sizes for where the load is going.
